features.description: Polish the armed-terminal hazard chrome on the existing component: token-only colours (no raw hex), persistent hazard frame while armed, role=alert + aria-live, a scope label, and a disarm-only affordance. OFF by default; no PTY/backend or command-channel change.
features.acceptance: armed-terminal renders disarmed by default with no hazard frame; when armed it shows a persistent hazard frame, role=alert, an explicit scope label, and only a disarm control; all colours come from tokens (no raw hex in the component); no new backend/exec call is introduced.

features.description: Bridge the legacy core stylesheet colour variables to the design tokens under data-theme/data-density so a theme or density swap survives onto legacy pages, without redesigning any page. Bridge layer carries no raw hex.
features.acceptance: a token bridge maps the legacy core stylesheet colour variables (background, text, border) onto the design-token layer; toggling data-theme or data-density changes the resolved legacy values; legacy pages re-colour without per-page edits; the bridge layer contains no raw hex.

features.description: Generalize the cockpit 5-state classifier into one reusable surface-state module (loading/missing/stale/error/ready) plus a shared render contract applied across the key surfaces, aligned to freshness.js thresholds. One classifier, many renderers; render-truth preserved (stale demoted, error shows last-good + retry).
features.acceptance: a pure surface_state classifier returns one of loading/missing/stale/error/ready for each key surface from its inputs; a shared renderer turns each state into the right chrome (skeleton/empty/stale-banner/error-retry/ready); stale is never rendered as fresh; the matrix is unit-tested across all five states for every key surface.

features.description: Journey tests that boot the real dashboard shell (createJarvis().init()) and drive each key surface through all five surface states using producer-shaped fixtures, asserting the shell renders the correct state chrome end-to-end.
features.acceptance: a journey test boots createJarvis().init() and, per key surface, feeds producer-shaped fixtures for each of loading/missing/stale/error/ready and asserts the rendered shell shows the matching state chrome; the theme/density swap and armed-terminal chrome are exercised through the real shell, not a synthetic mount.
